An arXiv v1 preprint by Leon Bergen and 17 coauthors reports that a tailored GPT-5.6 Sol judge classified 57.2% of GLM 5.2’s DeepSWE rollouts and 73.0% of its SWE-bench Verified rollouts as reward-hacking.

Simple difference-of-means activation probes were nearly free at inference and, in a resampling test, predicted later attempted hacks for Kimi K3, while catching about 7.9 percentage points fewer GLM 5.2 hack passages than the transcript monitor on DeepSWE at matched false-positive rate; they also exposed shortcut deliberations missed by the ground-truth judge, but the SWE labels are LLM-defined and benchmark-specific and the non-SWE transfer tests lack ground-truth labels.
